newsitem.title: USA: Exxon in pact for oil production in Chad.
newsitem.headline: Exxon in pact for oil production in Chad.

text.p: Exxon Corp said Friday it reached a pact with government of Chad on development terms for the first commercial oil production in that country.

A consortium headed by its affiliate, Esso Exploration and Production Chad Inc, settled key financial, legal and operating terms under which the Doba Basin project in southern Chad would be developed, Exxon said.
The total cost of developing the reserves and the infrastructure needed to transport them is expected to be in the range of about $3 billion.
The project area, located about 350 miles south of Chad's capital, N'Djamena, contains about 900 million barrels of recoverable reserves, Exxon said.

Esso is operator for the consortium and holds a 40 percent interest, while Royal Dutch/Shell Group affiliate Societe Shell Tchadienne de Recherches et d'Exploitation and Elf Aquitaine affiliate Elf Hydrocarbures Tchad hold 40 percent and 20 percent interests, respectively.
The project remains subject to final government ratification and financing.
In the interim, the consortium will invite proposals from potential bidders for the major engineering, procurement and construction contracts.
The Doba Basin Project would draw on reserves from three oil fields in southern Chad.
About 300 wells would be drilled, with peak production projected to be about 200-250 thousand barrels of oil per day, beginning as early as the year 2000, Exxon said.
The pact also outlines a second potential project in Chad.

That project would call for development of the Sedigi field north of Lake Chad and a pipeline to supply a refinery to be built in the capital city of N'Djamena and to be operated by Societe d'Etude et d'Exploitation de la Raffinerie du Tchad.
The refinery would produce fuel for transportation, electric power generation and other uses.
